title: Concept of Depreciation and the Straight-Line Method

back: [[imp:The systematic allocation of an asset's cost over its useful life.]]
It matches the asset's expense to the revenue it generates each period.
It does **not** measure decline in market value.
The portion of the asset's cost that will be expensed over time.
$$\text{Depreciable Cost} = \text{Asset Cost} - \text{Residual Value}$$
It is the total amount to be depreciated.
The undepreciated portion of the asset's cost.
$$\text{Book Value} = \text{Asset Cost} - \text{Accumulated Depreciation}$$
It cannot fall below residual value.

cards.front: What is the formula for [[kw:straight-line depreciation]]?
back: $$\text{Annual Depreciation} = \frac{\text{Cost} - \text{Residual Value}}{\text{Useful Life}}$$
Allocates an equal amount of expense to each full year.
The most widely used method by U.S. companies.

cards.front: Calculate annual straight-line depreciation: cost $15,000, residual $3,000, life 6 years.

back: Columns: Year, Cost, Depreciation Expense, Accumulated Depreciation, Book Value.
Each year: expense = annual depreciation; accumulated = sum of expenses so far; book = cost – accumulated.
Final book value must equal residual value.
cards.front: How do you build a [[kw:depreciation schedule]]?

back: $$\text{Partial Depreciation} = \text{Annual Depreciation} \times \frac{\text{Months in Service}}{12}$$
Used when an asset is purchased partway through the fiscal year.
The remaining depreciation extends into a later year.

cards.front: Annual depreciation is $3,000. Asset bought on May 1. First-year depreciation? (calendar-year company)
back: Months used: May–Dec = 8 months.
First-year depreciation = $3,000 × 8/12 = $2,000.
